summary: Hostile audit #17 — themes/manager.py, the CRUD-and-draft module wearing a themes label

survived.title: overwrite_theme WIPES the target theme's entire palette when the vacuum has no active theme — ok:True, persisted, no undo
survived.mechanism: overwrite_theme never reads the TARGET entry's content. It builds `resolved` from `active_entry = library.get(vac['active_theme_id'])` merged with the working draft (lines 302-308), then assigns that wholesale to theme['library'][theme_id]['tokens'/'colors'/'alpha'] (311-324). When the vacuum has no active theme (a never-touched vacuum — `_get_vacuum_theme` seeds active_theme_id=None; or any vacuum whose active theme was just deleted, since delete_theme:393 nulls the pointer) and the draft is empty, `_resolved_theme_payload(active_entry=None, draft={})` returns three empty dicts and the target's whole palette is replaced with {}. VERIFIED by executing the real module: import theme 'MyBaby' with tokens/colors/alpha populated, then `overwrite_theme(vacuum_entity_id='vacuum.robo', theme_id=<MyBaby>)` on a fresh vacuum returns {'ok': True, ...} and leaves {"name": "MyBaby", "tokens": {}, "colors": {}, "alpha": {}}. themes/services.py:169-178 then calls _raise_if_failed (no-op, ok is True) and `await manager.async_save()`, so the emptied theme is written to storage.
survived.user_impact: A single `eufy_vacuum.overwrite_theme` service call (documented service, callable from any automation/script/dev-tools) permanently empties a named, hand-authored theme. The service reports success, the card shows no error, and there is no undo or backup — the theme survives as a name with no palette.
survived.guards_checked: themes/manager.py:300-301 (only guard is `theme_id not in library`, i.e. existence of the TARGET — it never checks that the SOURCE, the active entry, exists or is non-empty); `_resolved_theme_payload`:195-210 (normalizes None into empty dicts rather than rejecting); `_normalize_theme_entry`:137 (accepts non-dict/None, returns blanks); themes/services.py:134-142 `_raise_if_failed` (only fires on ok=False, which this path never returns); src/bindings/theme.js:1176-1191 — the card's Save button only reaches overwriteTheme inside `if (state.activeThemeId)`, so the card masks the bug and it is reachable only via the service, which nothing else guards.
confirmations: CONFIRMED from source. overwrite_theme (manager.py:302-308) builds `resolved` from library.get(vac['active_theme_id']) + draft and never reads the target entry; lines 311-324 assign that wholesale to theme['library'][theme_id]. _resolved_theme_payload -> _normalize_theme_entry(None) (135-144) returns blank dicts rather than rejecting, so with no active theme and an empty draft the target's tokens/colors/alpha become {}. Only guard is `theme_id not in library` (300). services.py:169-178 _raise_if_failed cannot fire on ok=True and then awaits async_save, so the emptied entry is persisted. Card is not the vector (bindings/theme.js save handler only calls overwriteTheme inside `if (state.activeThemeId)` and passes that same id). DOWNGRADE HIGH->MEDIUM: identical root cause to CRUD-2 (which the same area rated MEDIUM), and reachable only via a hand-written service call with a parameter combination the card never produces — 'narrower conditions' per the stated ceiling. Damage is real (authored palette destroyed, ok:true, persisted, no undo), so it is not lower than MEDIUM.

REPRODUCED by executing the real module. import 'MyBaby' with tokens/colors/alpha -> overwrite_theme(vacuum_entity_id='vacuum.robo', theme_id=<MyBaby>) on a vacuum whose active_theme_id is None returns {'ok': True, 'theme_id': ..., 'active_theme_id': ..., 'draft_dirty': False} and the stored entry becomes {'id':..., 'name':'MyBaby', 'tokens':{}, 'colors':{}, 'alpha':{}, 'source':'manual'}. Root cause confirmed at manager.py:303-308: `resolved` is built from the ACTIVE entry + draft, never from the target; _resolved_theme_payload turns active_entry=None into three empty dicts (195-210) rather than refusing. services.py:176-177 runs _raise_if_failed (no-op on ok=True) then `await manager.async_save()`, so the emptied palette is persisted. Card is not the vehicle - src/bindings/theme.js:1176-1181 only reaches overwriteTheme inside `if (state.activeThemeId)` - but eufy_vacuum.overwrite_theme is a registered, documented service (services.yaml:2016) callable from dev-tools or any automation. services.yaml's own text 'Replace an existing library theme with a vacuum's current working draft' is contradicted by the code. HIGH is correct against the ceiling: one named authored theme is destroyed with no undo and no error - not the whole library, so not CRITICAL.

survived.title: overwrite_theme replaces the target with a copy of a DIFFERENT theme (the vacuum's active one), and silently repoints the vacuum at the target
survived.mechanism: Same root as CRUD-1: the content written to `theme_id` is the resolved ACTIVE theme + draft, never the target's own values. The docstring claims 'Overwrite an existing library entry with the vacuum's working draft' — it actually writes active-theme values the draft never contained. VERIFIED: themes A={'--x':'AAA'} and B={'--x':'BBB'}; set_active(A); `overwrite_theme(vacuum, theme_id=B)` with an EMPTY draft returns ok:True and B becomes {'--x':'AAA'} — B's authored palette is gone and B is now a byte-for-byte clone of A. Lines 326-328 additionally set vac['active_theme_id'] = theme_id, so the vacuum silently stops using A and starts using B.
survived.user_impact: An automation or dev-tools call naming any theme other than the currently active one destroys that theme's palette, replacing it with a duplicate of the active theme, and moves the vacuum onto it. Reported as success; nothing in the response distinguishes 'saved your edits' from 'cloned A over B'.
survived.guards_checked: themes/manager.py:300-301 (target existence only); no comparison of theme_id against vac['active_theme_id']; no check that the draft is non-empty (the method is named for the draft but does not require one); themes/services.py:169-178 (pass-through, saves); src/bindings/theme.js:1179 (card always passes state.activeThemeId, so the card never exercises the divergence and it is untested in practice).
confirmations: CONFIRMED and it is the general statement of CRUD-1. manager.py:303-308 resolves against active_id, not theme_id; 311-324 writes that over the named target; 326-328 then repoints vac['active_theme_id'] at the target. Nothing compares theme_id to active_theme_id and nothing requires a non-empty draft, despite the docstring at 297 claiming the write comes from the working draft. Metadata loop 321-323 preserves the target's name/source/tags, which is exactly why the result looks legitimate. Severity MEDIUM is correctly calibrated: service-only reachability, no robot impact, but real destruction of an authored theme reported as success. CRUD-1 and CRUD-2 are ONE defect and one fix.

REPRODUCED. A={'--x':'AAA'}, B={'--x':'BBB'}; set_active_theme(vacuum, A); overwrite_theme(vacuum, theme_id=B) with an EMPTY draft returns ok:True and B becomes {'name':'B','tokens':{'--x':'AAA'},...} - a clone of A - and the vacuum's active_theme_id is silently repointed to B (manager.py:326). Same root as CRUD-1 (line 303-309 resolves the ACTIVE entry, never `existing`), so this is one defect with two manifestations; fix once and both close. Impact is in fact equal to CRUD-1 (an authored palette destroyed, ok:True, persisted at services.py:177), but I am leaving the rating at MEDIUM deliberately so the campaign roll-up does not double-count one bug as two HIGHs. Nothing here touches dispatch - no robot behaviour is affected.

survived.title: delete_theme of a bundled/core theme is silently undone at the next HA restart — the seeder re-adds it
survived.mechanism: delete_theme does `del theme['library'][theme_id]` with no notion of provenance — it will delete an entry whose source is 'core'. ThemeManager.__init__:68 calls `ensure_preloaded_theme_library`, which (preloaded.py:525-535) re-seeds every spec whose id is NOT present in the library. There is no tombstone/deleted-ids list, so a deleted bundled id is indistinguishable from a never-seeded one. VERIFIED: delete_theme('theme_signal') removes it and the service persists the deletion; round-tripping the data through JSON and constructing a new ThemeManager (what an HA restart does) brings theme_signal back. src/renderers/theme.js:511-518 renders the delete button on every preset card except the one matching defaultThemeId, so 7 of the 8 bundled themes are deletable straight from the card UI.
survived.user_impact: A user who curates their preset grid by deleting bundled themes they will never use sees them all reappear after any HA restart or integration reload, with no error and no explanation. The action can never be completed, only repeated.
survived.guards_checked: themes/manager.py:379-397 (no source/'core' check, no tombstone written); preloaded.py:514-542 `ensure_preloaded_theme_library` (re-seed condition is purely `theme_id in library`; the only migration branch just backfills source); preloaded.py:544-546 (default_theme_id is also force-reset to theme_follow_ha); themes/services.py:202-208 (raises only on ok=False, which delete returns only for a missing id); src/renderers/theme.js:511 (gates the delete button on defaultThemeId only, not on source==='core').
confirmations: CONFIRMED both halves. delete_theme (386) does a bare `del theme['library'][theme_id]` with no provenance check and writes no tombstone; ensure_preloaded_theme_library (preloaded.py:525-535) re-seeds any spec whose id is absent, and its only in-place branch setdefaults 'source' then continues. ThemeManager.__init__:68 runs that seeder on every construction, i.e. every restart/reload. The card exposes the vector: renderers/theme.js gates the delete button only on `id !== state.defaultThemeId`, so every bundled theme except the default is deletable from the preset grid. MEDIUM is right — an action that silently cannot be completed, no data loss.

REPRODUCED end-to-end including the restart. delete_theme(theme_id='theme_signal') removes it (manager.py:386 `del`, no provenance check, no tombstone); round-tripping data through JSON and constructing a fresh ThemeManager - exactly what an HA restart does, since __init__:68 calls ensure_preloaded_theme_library - puts theme_signal back. preloaded.py:527-535 re-seeds on `theme_id not in library` with no deleted-ids list, so a deleted bundled id is indistinguishable from a never-seeded one. There are 8 PRELOADED_THEME_SPECS and src/renderers/theme.js:510-518 renders the delete button on every preset card except the one whose id == state.defaultThemeId, so 7 of 8 are deletable straight from the UI. One correction to the finder's write-up: preloaded.py:544-546 does NOT force-reset default_theme_id unconditionally - it only sets theme_follow_ha when the stored default is empty or no longer in the library (which is what happens after deleting the default). MEDIUM is right: nothing is lost, the action simply never sticks.

survived.title: overwrite_theme can permanently replace a bundled theme's palette while preserving source:"core", so user content keeps claiming to be shipped
survived.mechanism: overwrite_theme has no provenance guard, so `theme_id='theme_signal'` (a bundled entry) is a legal target. Lines 318-323 then deliberately carry `source` forward from the existing entry, so the rewritten entry keeps source:'core'. Unlike delete (CRUD-3), the id is still present, so `ensure_preloaded_theme_library` (preloaded.py:527) takes the `continue` branch and never restores the shipped values. VERIFIED: after overwrite_theme(theme_id='theme_signal') the entry is {"name": "Signal", "tokens": {"--x": "MINE"}, ..., "source": "core"} and it is still that after a simulated restart. Note import_theme:558-561 explicitly refuses to honor an incoming 'core' precisely because 'only the seeded preloaded themes are truly bundled' — overwrite_theme violates that same invariant from the inside.
survived.user_impact: The shipped Signal/High Contrast/Colorblind Safe palettes can be replaced by arbitrary user content that the gallery still labels and filters as a bundled 'core' theme, and the shipped version is unrecoverable except by the non-obvious delete-then-restart sequence. A user who exports and shares it ships their own palette under the bundled theme's name and provenance.
survived.guards_checked: themes/manager.py:291-336 (no check of existing.get('source') before overwriting); themes/manager.py:318-323 (the metadata-preservation loop is what propagates 'core'); preloaded.py:527-535 (id-present branch never restores content, only setdefaults 'source'); themes/manager.py:558-561 (the import path's contrasting 'never honor core' rule, which proves the invariant is intended); themes/services.py:169-178 (no provenance policy at the service layer).
confirmations: CONFIRMED. overwrite_theme has no `source`/read-only check, and the metadata-preservation loop (321-323) explicitly carries `source` forward, so a rewritten bundled entry keeps source:'core'. Because the id still exists, preloaded.py:527-535 takes the `continue` branch forever and never restores shipped content — there is no restore service in services.py. The contrast the finder cites is real: import_theme:557-561 deliberately refuses to honour an incoming 'core'. So the invariant is stated in-module and violated from the inside. MEDIUM correct (mislabelled provenance + unrecoverable bundled palette; no robot impact).

REPRODUCED. update_working_draft(tokens={'--x':'MINE'}) then overwrite_theme(theme_id='theme_signal') leaves {'name':'Signal','source':'core','tokens':{'--x':'MINE'}} and it is STILL that after a simulated restart, because preloaded.py:527 takes the `continue` branch for any id already present and never compares or restores content. The `source` survives because manager.py:321-323 deliberately carries metadata forward. import_theme:557-561 refusing to honour an incoming 'core' proves the invariant is intended, and overwrite_theme breaks it from the inside. The finder UNDERSTATED reachability: this is not service-only. Clicking a bundled preset sets active_theme_id to that core id, after which the card's footer Save button reads 'Save changes' (src/renderers/theme.js:1130-1133, hasActiveTheme true) and routes to overwriteTheme - so the ordinary 'pick Signal, tweak a colour, Save' flow permanently overwrites a shipped theme in place with no 'save a copy' prompt and no restore path. MEDIUM holds: the user did press Save on that theme, so it is missing core-protection rather than surprise destruction.

survived.mechanism: delete_theme:391-394 clears active_theme_id for every vacuum pointing at the deleted theme, but only RE-NORMALIZES working_draft — it never clears it and never clears draft_dirty. VERIFIED: after set_active(D) + update_working_draft(colors={'--y':'EDIT'}) + delete_theme(D), the vacuum state is {"active_theme_id": null, "working_draft": {"colors": {"--y": "EDIT"}}, "draft_dirty": true}. Every other path that changes what a vacuum is editing DOES clear the draft (set_active_theme:417, save_theme_as_new:277, overwrite_theme:327), so this is the one asymmetric exit. Downstream, `_resolved_theme_payload(active_entry=None, draft=...)` yields the draft alone, and src/bindings/theme.js:1173-1189 sees activeThemeId falsy so the Save button routes to saveThemeAsNew — which calls save_theme_as_new, whose `resolved` is again draft-only (manager.py:258-263).
survived.user_impact: After deleting the theme they were editing, the user still sees unsaved-edit state; clicking Save prompts for a name and creates a theme containing ONLY the handful of tokens they touched, silently dropping the entire base palette they believed they were editing. No error at any step.
survived.guards_checked: themes/manager.py:391-394 (loop nulls active_theme_id, calls _normalize_theme_draft, does not reset it or draft_dirty); revert_draft:466-478 (would clear it, but nothing calls it automatically); update_working_draft:454-457 (recomputes draft_dirty from bucket contents, so it stays True); src/bindings/theme.js:1220-1226 (delete handler confirms then only refreshes from backend — no draft reset).

Confirmed asymmetric: save_theme_as_new:277-278, overwrite_theme:327-328, set_active_theme:417-418 and revert_draft:470-471 all clear it; delete_theme is the lone exit that does not. Downstream claim also REPRODUCED: calling save_theme_as_new on that orphaned state writes a library theme containing only {'--y':'EDIT'} - the base palette the user believed they were editing is not in it. survived.title: rename_theme writes into the raw stored entry with no isinstance-dict guard, unlike set_theme_tags — a corrupt entry raises TypeError out of the service
survived.mechanism: rename_theme validates against the NORMALIZED view (`_get_theme_library_entries`), which turns any non-dict payload into a valid-looking entry (`_normalize_theme_entry`:137 `dict(payload) if isinstance(payload, dict) else {}`), then writes into the RAW store: `theme['library'][theme_id]['name'] = clean_name`. VERIFIED: with library['corrupt'] = 'oops', the normalized view reports the id as present and rename_theme raises TypeError: 'str' object does not support item assignment. set_theme_tags:367-368 does exactly the right thing here (`if not isinstance(entry, dict): return theme_not_found`), and delete_theme/overwrite_theme rebind the key rather than indexing into it, so rename is the lone unguarded writer. The same normalized-vs-raw split also strips keys (line 180), so a stored key with surrounding whitespace would pass the membership test and KeyError on the write.
survived.user_impact: An unhandled TypeError surfaces from the rename_theme service instead of a clean ServiceValidationError, if storage is ever corrupted or hand-edited. Latent — no in-tree path writes a non-dict library entry.
survived.guards_checked: themes/manager.py:347-348 (membership check is against the normalized copy, not the raw dict); _normalize_theme_entry:137 (deliberately tolerant, which is what makes the check pass); set_theme_tags:367-368 (the guard that exists elsewhere and is missing here); themes/services.py:180-189 (no try/except around the manager call).
confirmations: CONFIRMED as a latent robustness gap. rename_theme validates membership against the NORMALIZED copy (346-348) but writes into the raw store at 351, and _normalize_theme_entry:137 turns a non-dict payload into a valid-looking entry, so a corrupt entry passes the check and the write raises TypeError out of the service. set_theme_tags:365-368 has exactly the isinstance(entry, dict) guard that rename lacks; delete/overwrite rebind the key instead of indexing into it, so rename is genuinely the lone unguarded writer. The stripped-key KeyError variant is also real (_get_theme_library_entries:180 strips). No in-tree path writes a non-dict entry, so LOW is correct.

REPRODUCED both halves. With library['corrupt'] = 'oops', rename_theme(theme_id='corrupt', name='x') raises TypeError: 'str' object does not support item assignment, because the membership test at manager.py:347 runs against the NORMALIZED copy (_normalize_theme_entry:137 turns any non-dict into a valid-looking entry) while the write at 351 indexes the RAW store. The whitespace variant also reproduces: library[' spaced '] -> rename_theme(' spaced ') returns theme_not_found and rename_theme('spaced') raises KeyError: 'spaced', because _get_theme_library_entries:180 strips keys. set_theme_tags:367-368 has exactly the guard that is missing here, and delete/overwrite rebind the key rather than indexing into it, so rename is the only unguarded writer. No in-tree path writes a non-dict entry, so this is latent - it needs hand-edited or corrupted .storage. LOW is correct.

survived.title: delete_theme clears active_theme_id but leaves the deleted theme's working draft and draft_dirty in place — the orphan draft bleeds over the card's default look forever and survives restart
survived.mechanism: delete_theme walks every vacuum (lines 391-394) and does exactly two things: sets active_theme_id=None when it matched, and RE-NORMALISES working_draft. It never empties the draft and never clears draft_dirty. _get_vacuum_theme (line 123) then preserves draft_dirty verbatim (`bool(vac.get("draft_dirty", False))`), so the flag is sticky. Every sibling mutator that changes what a draft sits on top of does clear it — save_theme_as_new (277-278), overwrite_theme (327-328), set_active_theme (417-418), revert_draft (470-471) — delete_theme is the one that was forgotten, and line 394 proves the author had the draft in hand and only normalised it. The card applies the working draft unconditionally with no active-theme gate (src/state/theme.js:452-465, step 2 OVERLAY runs whether or not step 1 BASE found a theme), so the orphan keys paint on top of the card's built-in defaults. Persisted: handle_delete_theme awaits async_save (services.py:207), so the orphan is written to storage and reloaded on every restart. The sensor faithfully reports the contradiction — native_value 'none' (sensor/theme.py:70) while draft_dirty is True (sensor/theme.py:91).
survived.user_impact: A user activates a theme, tweaks a dozen tokens in the editor, decides they do not want that theme and deletes it from the Themes grid (the card's confirm dialog says nothing about drafts, src/bindings/theme.js:1221). The card immediately drops to its default look — except for the dozen leftover tokens from the theme they just deleted, which keep overriding it on every browser and across every restart, with no theme selected to explain them. The footer's 'Discard' and 'Save as new' buttons stay enabled because they key off draft_dirty (src/renderers/theme.js:1042, 1120-1133) and the label flips to 'Save as new' because activeThemeId is null. If the user takes that offer, save_theme_as_new resolves against active_entry=None (manager.py:259) and writes a library theme containing ONLY those dozen orphan keys, ok:true, no warning. The only cure is pressing Discard, which nothing tells them to do.

import_theme cannot shadow or overwrite a preloaded/core theme id: the payload's own `id` is discarded and a fresh id is always generated (manager.py:574). An import can only ADD a library entry, never replace one. The full-import path has no del/pop and no write to an existing key.

import_theme `source` laundering is correct and matches its comment: `core` is refused on import and downgraded to `manual` (manager.py:560-561), so an imported copy of a bundled theme cannot claim core provenance.

export_theme is a pure read: it takes the normalized copy from _get_theme_library_entries and never mutates the library; correspondingly handle_export_theme (services.py:242-247) is the only theme handler with no async_save, which is right.

Every MUTATING theme service does persist — handle_save/overwrite/rename/set_tags/delete/set_active/update_draft/revert/import all `await manager.async_save()` (services.py:166-257).
